title: Al-Ihkam fi Usul al-Ahkam (al-Amidi)
author: al-amidi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Sayf al-Din al-Amidi's comprehensive treatise on legal theory, which states every position with its arguments and objections before reaching a judgement. It is one of the most rigorous works of the theologians' school of usul.
historicalContext: Al-Amidi trained as a Hanbali in Iraq, became a Shafi'i, and taught in Cairo and Damascus. His Ihkam and its abridgement by Ibn al-Hajib shaped the teaching of usul in the Mamluk period.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
